<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-564e95e5f10725e6">Why use agent phase in KV eviction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aagentkv">AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different phases read different history. Representatives help assess future usefulness beyond current few accesses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early plan can regain importance during final reporting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:agentkv" data-paper-title="AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-df79f24c8c97731f">Why keep representative queries from several agent phases for KV eviction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aagentkv">AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Planning, tools, and reporting need different evidence. Recent queries alone may underrate material needed later. Phase representatives broaden retention scoring but cannot recover deleted KV or guarantee representativeness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tool arguments dominate recent access, but the final summary still needs the original task constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14872">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.14872-agentkv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-df79f24c8c97731f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:agentkv" data-paper-title="AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a76e1843a80ebe6c">How does a phase-aware buffer differ from a recent window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aagentkv">AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A recent window uses time. Phase-aware scoring compares history with representatives from multiple phases. It may preserve older evidence but is limited by budget and representative quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An old plan outside the window can still be retained when a phase query matches it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14872">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.14872-agentkv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a76e1843a80ebe6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:agentkv" data-paper-title="AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">

<h2 id="qa-f9b532269229b1e0">Does local phase-aware scoring modify SGLang&#x27;s real KV manager?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aagentkv">AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retained indices alone do not prove GPU memory was freed and read correctly.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:awq" data-paper-title="AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-awq-9367c7ce" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1a4162d95cfb1d5">Why use activations instead of weight magnitude alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aawq">AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / NVIDIA / Harvard / SJTU</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Output error depends on input activation. Calibration identifies salient channels and equivalent scaling protects them before uniform low-bit weight-only quantization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same weight error is more consequential when multiplied by large activations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1a4162d95cfb1d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:awq" data-paper-title="AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1ecb6d714c57abd">Why use equivalent scaling in AWQ rather than separately storing a few higher-precision weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aawq">AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / NVIDIA / Harvard / SJTU</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calibration activations identify output-sensitive input channels. Reciprocal input/weight scaling preserves the float function while making those weights easier to represent in one low-bit format. Large weights alone do not determine sensitivity, and KV growth is unrelated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal weight errors have different output effects on channels with small versus large activations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1ecb6d714c57abd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:awq" data-paper-title="AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-aedd4f3cf22864ab">What does AWQ add over round-to-nearest W4?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aawq">AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / NVIDIA / Harvard / SJTU</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search activation-aware equivalent channel scales before W4 rounding. RTN uses the given scale and nearest grid. Both can retain a uniform low-bit format.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rescale an important channel before rounding rather than round original weights directly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aedd4f3cf22864ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:awq" data-paper-title="AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ef8b97ca8a3077d">Must input be inversely scaled when weights are scaled by S?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aawq">AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / NVIDIA / Harvard / SJTU</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes: XW=(XS⁻¹)(SW). Without reciprocal scaling the floating function already changes. Search scales by quantized reconstruction error; local MSE does not establish TinyChat throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiply one weight channel by two and divide its input by two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ef8b97ca8a3077d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bakron" data-paper-title="BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-bakron-8758065a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-123e76370ee763fb">Why isn&#x27;t BaKron ordinary elementwise rounding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abakron">BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It minimizes curvature-weighted joint error, not distance to each scalar grid point. Correlated rounding errors can amplify or cancel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two small errors aligned in one output can be worse than a larger pair that cancels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.06291-bakron/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-123e76370ee763fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bakron" data-paper-title="BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb4b0da0ce3093eb">Why use bilateral Kronecker curvature instead of input activation alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abakron">BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Output-side curvature also changes the impact of weight error. A Kronecker approximation includes both sides in a quadratic objective, with structured parallel/divide-and-conquer rounding instead of a full Hessian. Independent rounding is not equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal input errors can differ in loss sensitivity along different output directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.06291-bakron/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb4b0da0ce3093eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bakron" data-paper-title="BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-372536e06264d80f">What does BaKron add over input-side GPTQ-style rounding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abakron">BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight vectorized error with A⊗B to include both curvatures. Optimization must match that bilateral objective; row-wise rounding is not equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lower ordinary MSE can still incur greater bilateral weighted error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.06291-bakron/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-372536e06264d80f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bakron" data-paper-title="BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c531490304feada">Why check vectorization order and Kronecker factors together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abakron">BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Flattening convention determines which side each factor acts on. Swapped axes optimize a different error. Compare an explicit vectorized reference; random small weights are not checkpoint-scale evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Row- and column-major flattening require consistent factor conventions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.06291-bakron/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c531490304feada">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:beaconkv" data-paper-title="BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-beaconkv-c9b2fe88" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfdbd7560ad2b7ec">Why retain representative queries in addition to recent ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abeaconkv">BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hanyang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long reasoning may revisit an early plan. Beacons cover diverse attention directions for budgeted retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The last few queries can miss the original instruction needed at the end.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04971">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04971-beaconkv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfdbd7560ad2b7ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:beaconkv" data-paper-title="BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c86ea72842083a1">How does BeaconKV preserve plans that recent-only queries would evict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abeaconkv">BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hanyang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Maintain a small set of representative historical beacons, score KV across phases, and protect a recent window. Representatives approximate future access, not guarantee all distant evidence survives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten arithmetic steps may ignore an opening constraint that the final answer needs; a beacon can keep it important.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:beaconkv" data-paper-title="BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b76b212b862402f">How does beacon scoring differ from evicting by age?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abeaconkv">BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hanyang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Age assumes newer is better. Beacon scoring uses query-space coverage and key matches, plus recent protection. It can still miss evidence and is not a future-query oracle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An old KV matching a planning query may outlast irrelevant old entries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04971">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04971-beaconkv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b76b212b862402f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:beaconkv" data-paper-title="BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dccffec6bb5d9e58">Why count the Python selector and backing cache in system costs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abeaconkv">BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hanyang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selection and indexing may be expensive, and retaining full backing cache does not free GPU memory. Public checkpoint tests saw slowdown and quality loss; report quality, working set, and full cost separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 512-item attention set can still keep all KV and spend time scoring it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04971">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04971-beaconkv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dccffec6bb5d9e58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:c2kv" data-paper-title="C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-c2kv-5a6eab64" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-056757cd116bea34">Why make compressed C²KV both short and reusable by concatenation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ac2kv">C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short single-segment cache does not guarantee combined use. Train compression tokens and structured attention for both compression and reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse several compressed fragments on a new query rather than prefill them again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17715">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17715-c2kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-056757cd116bea34">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:c2kv" data-paper-title="C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-325fef9068a4285a">Why jointly train compression and concatenation reuse in C²KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ac2kv">C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independently compressed KV can depend on original positions or context. Compression tokens and structured attention train representations that work together across segments. This still has information loss and interface constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two compressed documents should jointly supply evidence, not only reconstruct individually.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17715">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17715-c2kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-325fef9068a4285a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:c2kv" data-paper-title="C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-24bcb420d94c7597">How does joint training differ from compressing each segment and arbitrarily concatenating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ac2kv">C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint training accounts for position-independent composition. Independent compression can lose cross-segment evidence. Equal compression ratios do not imply equal concatenation behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two fragments can answer local questions individually yet fail cross-fragment queries when combined.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17715">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17715-c2kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24bcb420d94c7597">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:c2kv" data-paper-title="C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b33edaf19feb7824">What interface checks matter between Extractor output and concatenated input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ac2kv">C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify per-segment Z shape, concatenation boundaries, and structured attention visibility. Local mini-suite omits paper-scale training and kernels; concatenability alone is insufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct lengths with wrong boundaries can cause reads from the wrong segment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17715">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17715-c2kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b33edaf19feb7824">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:distillcache" data-paper-title="DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-distillcache-374f7173" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e565b459c75c1f5">Why treat KV eviction as a multistep decision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adistillcache">DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Oklahoma State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A deletion changes later available history. Local salience may not predict future loss. Stepwise full-versus-evicted KL trains a policy for later prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A currently unused KV can become answer evidence and may not be recoverable after deletion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.08878-distillcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e565b459c75c1f5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:distillcache" data-paper-title="DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-58b3581acbd44eb8">Why reward predictive KL rather than token deletions in DistillCache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adistillcache">DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Oklahoma State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deletion is a resource action; retaining predictive information is the goal. Compare full and evicted distributions per step so the policy can trade behavior loss against budget. The reference is training-only, and low KL is not universally lossless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Padding and a key ID both save one KV, but only the latter may sharply change next-token probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.08878-distillcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58b3581acbd44eb8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:distillcache" data-paper-title="DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c79858649dfff33">Would KL-guided and minimum-cache rewards prefer the same policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adistillcache">DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Oklahoma State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not generally. One penalizes prediction drift; the other rewards space. Compare at fixed budget or explicit quality limits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Deleting all KV minimizes cache but can strongly change predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.08878-distillcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c79858649dfff33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:distillcache" data-paper-title="DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-013b0bbdf970cea9">How sanity-check DistillCache&#x27;s negative KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adistillcache">DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Oklahoma State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal distributions yield zero. Larger KL gives a lower reward. Use −KL(p_full||p_evict), not the reverse or a positive sign. Mini-suite does not prove policy training or deployment gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving evicted predictions farther from full should not raise reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.08878-distillcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-013b0bbdf970cea9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:drop-kv" data-paper-title="DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-drop-kv-30cd8cec" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a600aaa84c0b9885">Why score removal by output perturbation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adrop-kv">DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University at Albany, SUNY</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight alone omits value geometry. Estimate each removal&#x27;s output change and aggregate across observed queries for eviction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-weight value close to the output may be safe to remove.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22130">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a600aaa84c0b9885">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:drop-kv" data-paper-title="DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec49fca15913baed">Why consider value versus current output rather than only attention weight in DropKV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adrop-kv">DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University at Albany, SUNY</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Removing a term removes its value and renormalizes the rest. Change depends on p/(1−p) times output–value difference. Unusual low-weight values can matter more than redundant high-weight ones; combining single scores is approximate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two tokens both weighted 0.1 can cause very different changes if one value equals the aggregate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22130">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec49fca15913baed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:drop-kv" data-paper-title="DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9915fdbd0fe30af8">Does exact single removal guarantee optimal multiple removal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adrop-kv">DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University at Albany, SUNY</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Joint removal renormalizes and interacts. Per-item ranking approximates the combination, and theoretical guarantees have conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two compensating values can each seem unimportant yet jointly change the output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22130">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9915fdbd0fe30af8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:drop-kv" data-paper-title="DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b8cc24761f32313">Does an epsilon preserve the formula when p_j rounds to one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adrop-kv">DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University at Albany, SUNY</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. p_j/(1−p_j) is singular, and local code rejects it. Check infinite recent protection, MaxPool, and averaging GQA scores into physical KV heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Epsilon makes a finite approximation, not the exact zero-denominator result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22130">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b8cc24761f32313">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dualquant" data-paper-title="DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-dualquant-6a91d161" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8048975d5ad6a4a1">How can DualQuant rescale activations without calibrating on them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adualquant">DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · d-Matrix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fit row/block and column scales from W alone. Apply learned column scales reciprocally to X at runtime. A solver that never reads X does not mean inference never transforms X.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Derive column scales offline, then rescale input channels before quantization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13767-dualquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8048975d5ad6a4a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dualquant" data-paper-title="DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-446916bce4be2de7">Why fit both row and column scales without calibration activations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adualquant">DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · d-Matrix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Row scaling cannot resolve shared outlier columns. Fit both to static weight reconstruction and use column scales for runtime activation rescaling. With fixed codes solve scalar least squares, project to legal scales, and requantize; code changes need not be monotone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A column large across many rows needs joint treatment and compatible input scaling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13767-dualquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-446916bce4be2de7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dualquant" data-paper-title="DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8a760545553a980">How does alternating closed-form scaling differ from heuristic exponent search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adualquant">DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · d-Matrix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate grid assignment and scales; solve scalar least squares at fixed codes, project to legal formats, and requantize. Heuristics do not implement this optimization or its conditional descent result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixed-code optimal scale must be reconsidered after codes change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13767-dualquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8a760545553a980">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dualquant" data-paper-title="DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4b9bed84b4d505b">Can column fitting use old codes after changing row inverse scales?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adualquant">DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · d-Matrix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Project row inverse scales, synchronize inner copies, and requantize before solving columns, then requantize again. The supported INT4 subset is not MXFP4.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fitting columns to stale codes violates alternating optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13767-dualquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4b9bed84b4d505b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:flint" data-paper-title="FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-flint-b6635740" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3cb4a3672d01e33f">Why compress both query and document to a fixed vector count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aflint">FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token-level multivector indexing and search grow with length. Separate learned latents produce fixed V vectors per side for explicit cost control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long and short documents can both yield four vectors, as can queries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27273v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.27273-flint/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3cb4a3672d01e33f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:flint" data-paper-title="FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-10237052848a4d0f">Why isn&#x27;t FLINT score a symmetric mean similarity at fixed V?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aflint">FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Learned latents read tokens on both sides. Score each query latent by its best document match, then sum across queries. Fixed budgets do not make pooling arbitrary or scoring symmetric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Location and time query latents each find evidence; reversing which side is summed generally changes the score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27273v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.27273-flint/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10237052848a4d0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:flint" data-paper-title="FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-34f7e79c24287723">How does latent pooling differ from truncation or averaging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aflint">FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cross-attention reads all valid tokens before residuals and FFN, producing task-relevant fixed-budget vectors. Truncation loses tails and means use different aggregation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A latent can attend to a fact at the end that first-four truncation never sees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27273v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.27273-flint/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-34f7e79c24287723">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:flint" data-paper-title="FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e80b8d317da141cf">Why define FLINT padding masks and fully masked inputs explicitly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aflint">FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Padding cannot participate in cross-attention; local True denotes valid tokens and wholly masked rows fail. Preserve pre-LN and both residual stages, not a bare attention pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Padding half a batch must not change what latents read.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27273v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.27273-flint/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e80b8d317da141cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:fpot" data-paper-title="Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-fpot-d99f8a99" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e35f6580ad32c97e">Why insert half octaves in a power-of-two grid?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Afpot">Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Half-exponent spacing increases four-bit resolution, while odd exponents use 1.5 for shift-add. This trades accuracy and execution rather than allowing arbitrary floating values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A level near 1.5 is finer than only one or two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21257-fpot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e35f6580ad32c97e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:fpot" data-paper-title="Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-81d4a22b9952e7e2">Why calibrate on the deployed 1.5 approximation to √2 in FPoT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Afpot">Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exact half-exponent calibration followed by approximate execution adds unoptimized error. Choose scale and phase for the real shift-add grid. Integer shifts round, and activation/KV formats are separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A code calibrated at √2×scale runs at 1.5×scale; awareness lets calibration choose a better code or scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21257-fpot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-81d4a22b9952e7e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:fpot" data-paper-title="Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd311de36dfea355">Do FPoT weights, activations, and KV use one format?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Afpot">Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Weights use a half-octave grid; activations and KV use uniform integers. Account for each format and execution cost separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shift-add weight codes do not remove activation scaling rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21257-fpot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd311de36dfea355">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:fpot" data-paper-title="Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-24533125688bda58">Why subtract one from nonzero magnitude code m?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Afpot">Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Zero has a reserved code and m=e+1 otherwise. Recover e=m−1 for parity and shift. Signed right shifts can round, so do not claim exact real multiplication by 1.5.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Magnitude code one is e=0, not an odd exponent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21257-fpot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24533125688bda58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gqa" data-paper-title="GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-gqa-9496fcce" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-36f4e474bbcb6a45">Why share fewer K/V heads among more queries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agqa">GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Queries keep distinct directions while grouped history lowers cache and read bandwidth. It interpolates between per-head MHA and single-group MQA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four query heads can share two stored KV histories instead of four.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-36f4e474bbcb6a45">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gqa" data-paper-title="GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b644d6aec39b7b8b">Does GQA reduce Q heads or KV heads, and why does it save decode memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agqa">GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Many query heads share fewer K/V heads while retaining different queries. Each historical position stores and reads fewer KV groups. This reduces independence compared with MHA, not history token count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Eight queries can use two KV groups while producing eight different attention distributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b644d6aec39b7b8b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gqa" data-paper-title="GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-58190c8080d5c2fe">Which head-count axis distinguishes MHA, GQA, and MQA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agqa">GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MHA generally has one KV per Q, GQA shares within groups, and MQA shares globally. Query head count can remain fixed; quality and bandwidth are empirical.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep eight Q heads with eight, two, or one KV group.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
