</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gqa" data-paper-title="GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-16543b687401639e">Does temporarily expanding shared KV establish cache savings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agqa">GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Logical broadcast can aid compute, but persistent KV must store fewer groups; retaining expanded copies loses savings. Check g(h) and distinguish local from original uptraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four Q heads sharing two groups should store two histories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16543b687401639e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:irekogpt" data-paper-title="IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-irekogpt-3d6c018e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bdca470c192c241">Why expose nested widths from one checkpoint?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Airekogpt">IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One ordered basis supports several budget levels without separately stored pruned models. Width k takes its first k directions and receives calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Narrow and wide paths share the same ordered basis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00426">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00426-irekogpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bdca470c192c241">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:irekogpt" data-paper-title="IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a064a673ce4212b">Why retain projection bases for one IrekoGPT checkpoint to support nested widths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Airekogpt">IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dropping directions fixes width. Ordered bases let each width take a prefix, and multi-ratio calibration and linear correction reduce error. Shared structure does not equal shared quality or measured throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Switch between narrow and wide subnets only if extra basis directions were not discarded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00426">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00426-irekogpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a064a673ce4212b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:irekogpt" data-paper-title="IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8226754023f92bc6">How do nested widths differ from single-ratio pruning in deployment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Airekogpt">IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Single-ratio pruning retains one width. Nested storage and calibration allow runtime k selection, but do not guarantee every width&#x27;s quality or speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Validating k=64 does not validate k=32 automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00426">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00426-irekogpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8226754023f92bc6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:irekogpt" data-paper-title="IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5aef5e230352417b">Why not fit an independent projection basis per width?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Airekogpt">IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>W_k=P_:kᵀWP_:k requires prefixes of one basis. Independent choices break nesting. Preserve downstream linear calibration and ridge correction; local scope is subnet diagnosis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The 32-wide basis must be the first 32 directions of the 64-wide basis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00426">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00426-irekogpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5aef5e230352417b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kvmem" data-paper-title="KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-kvmem-cf5b3efc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d95f4ff4a7e079ef">Why page long agent histories as KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akvmem">KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai University of Finance and Economics</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History can exceed memory and context; summaries may lose details. KVMEM stores computed KV in tiers, indexes relevant blocks, and materializes a native-window view.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many pages can exist while only several are loaded per execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04852">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d95f4ff4a7e079ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kvmem" data-paper-title="KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d8a15b1ab7d92db2">Why doesn&#x27;t separating KVMEM&#x27;s address space from execution window mean all-history attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akvmem">KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai University of Finance and Economics</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Store paged KV across tiers, retrieve relevant blocks in attention space, and materialize a bounded native-window view. Missed evidence stays out. Local full backing cache and no complete async tiering mean no VRAM or speed claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Load a few old KV pages per query, not every page at once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04852">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d8a15b1ab7d92db2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kvmem" data-paper-title="KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc417fdf357b8f1d">How does paged KV reuse differ from retrieving text and prefilling it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akvmem">KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai University of Finance and Economics</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Paged reuse materializes computed K/V; text retrieval usually computes K/V again. Position, storage, and consistency contracts differ, so retrieval count alone is not cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fetch cached KV versus fetch tokens and calculate their KV anew.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04852">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc417fdf357b8f1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kvmem" data-paper-title="KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6cfc8c9db5b4d6e">Why not claim lower peak VRAM while retaining full backing cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akvmem">KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai University of Finance and Economics</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A bounded working set does not prove offload. Local Python retains backing cache and does not establish production kernels. Report working set, residency, movement, and end-to-end time separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading 512 of 2048 resident slots still occupies all 2048.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04852">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6cfc8c9db5b4d6e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:leapquant" data-paper-title="LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-leapquant-7df56645" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a08ab17fa09ca660">Why address both repeated rounding and state outliers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aleapquant">LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recurrence accumulates quantization error and outliers dominate scale. Window buffering reduces rounding frequency; high-precision compensation separates large directions before residual quantization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not recompress every token or let one direction consume the entire grid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38166">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.38166-leapquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a08ab17fa09ca660">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:leapquant" data-paper-title="LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d05f7382a4bdff1">Why buffer high-precision updates in a window instead of quantizing each step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aleapquant">LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repeated rounding feeds back into recurrence. Keep a low-bit base plus precise increments and requantize at boundaries; separate compensation protects outlier directions. Buffer and compensation cost memory. Local truncated SVD is not the original kernel or throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accumulate tiny updates before rounding so each is not lost individually.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38166">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.38166-leapquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d05f7382a4bdff1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:leapquant" data-paper-title="LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-513d646d0a8721ad">What is the trade-off between window buffers and low-bit writes every step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aleapquant">LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Buffers add temporary high-precision state but reduce whole-state requantization; stepwise writes round more often. Count base, updates, and compensation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Buffering eight updates before one quantization differs from eight whole-state writes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38166">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.38166-leapquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-513d646d0a8721ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:leapquant" data-paper-title="LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb3cdbcefb0ee551">Should the low-bit part quantize S or S−C?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aleapquant">LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Form C from truncated SVD, quantize S−C, then add C at readout. Quantizing full S and adding C counts it twice. Merge precise window updates at the prescribed boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An outlier direction stored in C need not be stored in full in the residual too.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38166">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.38166-leapquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb3cdbcefb0ee551">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moezip" data-paper-title="MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-moezip-03b66820" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed92465526edc741">Why connect KV error to MoE routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoezip">MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Eviction perturbs attention outputs seen by the router. Attention quality alone can miss route-sensitive positions, so estimate anchors from observed instruction gates and attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A nonmaximal KV can move a token across an expert boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30206v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30206-moezip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed92465526edc741">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moezip" data-paper-title="MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-88eb9936565008cf">Why reserve routing anchors in a normal MoE KV compression budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoezip">MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KV deletions can change attention and subsequent routing. Propagate Fisher sensitivity from observed instruction positions through attention, reserve anchors, then fill with the base compressor. Sensitivity is a proxy, not a route-flip guarantee or permission to read gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An older low-attention token can still affect expert choice and merit retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30206v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30206-moezip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88eb9936565008cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moezip" data-paper-title="MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1475de3e0254894">Is Fisher trace an exact top-k router flip criterion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoezip">MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It averages distribution curvature over directions and omits the router-to-hidden Jacobian. High trace does not imply a flip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal trace at two positions can yield different routing changes under different perturbation directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30206v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30206-moezip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1475de3e0254894">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moezip" data-paper-title="MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-86fa47a3c2433cb6">Can the base compressor select anchors again when filling budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoezip">MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Exclude already selected anchors and fill with distinct positions. Gather real KV in original temporal order. Use prefill instruction only, never future gold diagnostics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With 64 slots and 16 anchors, add 48 distinct non-anchor positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30206v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30206-moezip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86fa47a3c2433cb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pn-mix" data-paper-title="PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-pn-mix-d9cac8c7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ab7c9ef4cdc52767">Why assign higher precision to some RoPE pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apn-mix">PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rotation planes differ in QK impact. Prefill average Q/K norm products estimate importance, and each KV head fixes its high-precision set, trading cache width for attention error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve both dimensions of a high-impact rotation pair together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19605">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.19605-pn-mix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ab7c9ef4cdc52767">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pn-mix" data-paper-title="PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d6512262c17fb80">Why score true RoPE pairs with Q/K norm products rather than K magnitude alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apn-mix">PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Attention error depends on both query and key. Score each rotation plane jointly to preserve coupling. Choose high-precision pairs per shared KV head during prefill and reuse them without future decode data. Memory adjacency need not be a true pair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A large key direction rarely used by queries may not deserve precision; adjacent Llama channels need not rotate together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19605">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.19605-pn-mix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d6512262c17fb80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pn-mix" data-paper-title="PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e3767a853121441">Are PN-Mix 1-bit correction and FP16 residual buffering the same?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apn-mix">PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Correction shifts 1-bit reconstruction bins without extra residual codes. The buffer holds new not-yet-quantized tokens. They have distinct numerical and storage roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Corrected quantized groups can coexist with a new full-precision token batch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19605">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.19605-pn-mix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e3767a853121441">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pn-mix" data-paper-title="PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7968bfc3fd2d22c7">Can Llama/SmolLM2 RoPE pairs be formed from adjacent coordinates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apn-mix">PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No for split-half layout: pair corresponding coordinates across the halves, unlike interleaved layout. Pin the prefill-selected mask across pages, without decode lookahead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Pair index i in the first half with index i in the second, not necessarily i+1.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19605">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.19605-pn-mix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7968bfc3fd2d22c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:qevict" data-paper-title="QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-qevict-bcd29a04" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc8c66a9a9ec4980">Why have full, recoverable quantized, and deleted states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aqevict">QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The middle tier keeps dormant history available with less storage and supports promotion under renewed attention, unlike deletion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A previously irrelevant window can return to high-priority reading.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05326">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05326-qevict/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc8c66a9a9ec4980">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:qevict" data-paper-title="QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e5f2217749ab819">Why add a recoverable quantized tier between full precision and deletion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aqevict">QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Attention relevance can drift. Lower storage preserves approximate content for promotion when accumulated attention rises. Permanent deletion cannot recover it; dequantization does not restore lost precision. Local state checks are not serving performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Demote an old clue, then read it again when a later question needs it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05326">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05326-qevict/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e5f2217749ab819">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:qevict" data-paper-title="QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ec63ac32bc80f3b">Is promotion from quantized cache equivalent to never quantizing it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aqevict">QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not necessarily. Dequantization restores access, not every original bit. Measure quantization error separately from the advantage over deletion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Converting a low-bit vector to float does not restore original decimals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05326">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05326-qevict/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ec63ac32bc80f3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:qevict" data-paper-title="QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f1c01ec5ec98bd8">What should QEvict verify when cumulative scores update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aqevict">QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify decay γ, current attention increments, promotion threshold, and slot budget. Keep actual recoverable quantized content. A log state alone does not migrate data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Crossing τ should restore the stored vector, not just increment a count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05326">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05326-qevict/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f1c01ec5ec98bd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:race-rope-compression" data-paper-title="RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-race-rope-compression-5eb673ad" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-12c085821e363300">Why directly reduce native attention head width?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arace-rope-compression">RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT CSAIL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Low-rank storage followed by full reconstruction saves memory but adds work. RACE folds selections and V subspaces into projections so attention runs on retained dimensions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Run four-dimensional attention directly instead of rebuilding eight dimensions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28385v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28385-race-rope-compression/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12c085821e363300">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:race-rope-compression" data-paper-title="RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0fa836509cee57ad">Why keep original RoPE frequencies and head scaling after RACE narrows attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arace-rope-compression">RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT CSAIL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>This is a subspace of an existing model. Preserve complete matched Q/K rotation pairs, original frequencies and width scaling; fold V projections into weights for native low-dimensional compute. Calibration energy optimizes a bound, not global LM loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep original second and fifth frequencies rather than renumbering them first and second.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28385v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28385-race-rope-compression/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0fa836509cee57ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:race-rope-compression" data-paper-title="RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1418a84b5cb87943">Why compress Q/K in pairs but V with an SVD subspace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arace-rope-compression">RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT CSAIL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Q/K preserve common RoPE planes and matching geometry. Values carry aggregated content and can use a calibrated right singular space. One common pruning rule changes their roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep the corresponding K pair for each Q pair; V need not use those coordinates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28385v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28385-race-rope-compression/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1418a84b5cb87943">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:race-rope-compression" data-paper-title="RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4b009a69b7540d9">Why fold W_O when compressing V?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arace-rope-compression">RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT CSAIL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>W_V′=W_VP_V and W_O′=P_VᵀW_O define one subspace path. Changing V alone mismatches shape or function. Detach calibration and SVD while retaining gradients through folded forward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A four-dimensional V needs a matching output map, not the original eight-dimensional interpretation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28385v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28385-race-rope-compression/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4b009a69b7540d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:random-attention" data-paper-title="Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-random-attention-6364631b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd62a3fce54a9f29">Why omit KV importance scoring in Random Attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arandom-attention">Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce AI Research / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scoring costs compute and can impose one shared ranking. Protect the prompt and sample generated positions uniformly per head as a simpler cache trade-off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep part of each head&#x27;s history without scanning all tokens for importance first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03430">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.03430-random-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd62a3fce54a9f29">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:random-attention" data-paper-title="Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-11ce14334bb11855">Why protect full prompts but sample generated history independently per head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arandom-attention">Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce AI Research / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prompt preservation keeps task conditions and initial evidence fixed. Per-head random retention avoids scoring and gives diverse coverage, but may miss important reasoning and must fit the protected prompt budget. GPU reconstruction is not full task or kernel evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different heads can see different reasoning fragments while all still read the original question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03430">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.03430-random-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11ce14334bb11855">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:random-attention" data-paper-title="Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bda7ea99e557586e">How does independent per-head sampling differ from a shared random set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arandom-attention">Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce AI Research / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Head-specific sets vary evidence coverage; shared sampling applies one restriction everywhere. Average budgets can match while errors and coverage correlations differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One head can keep position five and another eight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03430">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.03430-random-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bda7ea99e557586e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:random-attention" data-paper-title="Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e7ddbb5a54699df">May the method drop prompt entries if B is smaller than prompt length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arandom-attention">Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce AI Research / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not under full prompt protection. B−|P| must be a valid generation budget. Raise the budget or report infeasibility rather than changing the method silently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-entry prompt cannot fit untouched into 80 slots.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:remote-kv-tiers" data-paper-title="When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-remote-kv-tiers-30f3c03e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e527c1e282435f7">Why analyze fetch versus re-prefill break-even first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aremote-kv-tiers">When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Multiverse Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Remote hits pay request and transfer costs; GPU recompute can be fast. Compare both paths by length and bandwidth, not only hit rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fetching a short cached prefix can be slower than recreating KV.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21500-remote-kv-tiers/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e527c1e282435f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:remote-kv-tiers" data-paper-title="When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a402f43cbcb16963">Why can a remote KV hit be slower than re-prefill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aremote-kv-tiers">When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Multiverse Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fetch has fixed request latency and volume-dependent transfer; recompute depends on prefill throughput. Break-even depends on length and bandwidth, and asynchronous shards must avoid head-of-line blocking. Hit rate is not latency. No local remote implementation or GPU results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short hit can spend more time opening the connection than local recompute takes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21500-remote-kv-tiers/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a402f43cbcb16963">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:remote-kv-tiers" data-paper-title="When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9793c53dde08a50">Does B&gt;sR with fixed T0 guarantee fetch is faster at every length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aremote-kv-tiers">When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Multiverse Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It gives asymptotic bandwidth advantage. Compare T0+sn/B against n/R for finite requests; fixed cost can dominate short ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fast per-token transfer does not erase first-packet latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21500-remote-kv-tiers/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9793c53dde08a50">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:remote-kv-tiers" data-paper-title="When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f0347ac1da13fce">Why use per-PCP-rank remote instances and async loading?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aremote-kv-tiers">When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Multiverse Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MLA cache is sharded by rank; independent instances and async loads reduce head-of-line blocking. Validation needs the multi-node service and workload, not a single A100/A30 fixture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A large request on one rank should not hold a small load on another.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21500-remote-kv-tiers/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f0347ac1da13fce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:replayssm" data-paper-title="ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-replayssm-704fd9a0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c13270329afc187">Why cache small inputs instead of writing a full matrix each token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areplayssm">ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matrix-state traffic can be bandwidth-bound. Refresh periodically and record inputs for reassociated reads, especially output-only speculative checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Store one anchor and several small inputs instead of a whole matrix per step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c13270329afc187">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:replayssm" data-paper-title="ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e28927a2b0831632">Why commit only accepted inputs and keep a high-precision anchor separate from low-precision reads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areplayssm">ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay outputs from a checkpoint and short input log without full writes every token. Rejected drafts cannot enter committed state. Refresh from the high-precision anchor and raw records to avoid rounding feedback. Reassociation preserves recurrence dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accept two of four drafts and advance only two steps; do not refresh from the rejected tail or rounded copy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e28927a2b0831632">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:replayssm" data-paper-title="ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4172e0c34881090a">How should output-only replay match stepwise recurrence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areplayssm">ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute equivalent readout without materializing each state. Persistent refresh uses only committed inputs. Computation and writes change, not the reference accepted sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Match ordinary recurrence on accepted tokens; rejected drafts affect neither committed state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4172e0c34881090a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:replayssm" data-paper-title="ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6a30bb586839092">Why preserve raw values and recompute residuals when refreshing GDN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areplayssm">ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residuals depend on the precise anchor. Reusing rounded reads or stale residuals feeds error back. Refresh from committed raw records and separately produce high/low copies; zero accepted tokens leave the anchor unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rejected drafts may have computed outputs without updating committed recurrence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6a30bb586839092">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:right-on-q" data-paper-title="Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-right-on-q-5ed3d308" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-015ce5e8dc05282d">Why let the quantized student generate training prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aright-on-q">Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Michigan, Ann Arbor</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Quantization changes visited reasoning states. Query the frozen teacher on the student&#x27;s actual states rather than fixed full-precision answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student takes a wrong turn, the teacher still scores the same prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29378v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.29378-right-on-q/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-015ce5e8dc05282d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:right-on-q" data-paper-title="Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fbeed3269c200615">Why distill on the quantized student&#x27;s prefixes with per-candidate KL mixing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aright-on-q">Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Michigan, Ann Arbor</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Quantization changes visited states, so score the student&#x27;s own prefixes. Teacher/student probability ratios mix forward and reverse KL per candidate to treat over- and underestimation differently. Detach mixture weights and retain a residual mass bucket.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct number underweighted and a connective overweighted at one position need different coefficients, not ideal teacher prefixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29378v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.29378-right-on-q/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fbeed3269c200615">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:right-on-q" data-paper-title="Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcd2b6d622a04412">How does candidate Dynamic KL differ from one fixed mixture per response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aright-on-q">Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Michigan, Ann Arbor</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>At a prefix, some candidates are underweighted and others overweighted. α_v adapts to p_v/q_v per candidate and is detached to avoid optimizing the weight itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Increasing support for one candidate and suppressing another need not share a mixture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29378v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.29378-right-on-q/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcd2b6d622a04412">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
